title: What happens on Kalshi when Bitcoin’s latest price and hourly average sit on opposite sides of the settlement cutoff?
author: woztrades
selftext:
I wanted to test an idea on the Kalshi’s 15 minute BTC market which looks for opportunities when the latest price and 1 hour VWAP of BTC sit on the opposite side at the settlement cutoff of the 15 minute market. The strategy would buy the side of the latest price when it was at least $25 from the cutoff and the 1 hour VWAP was at least $5 on the other side.  
  
I backtested the strategy and got a solid result back based on 30 days of historical data: +$41.52 PnL, max drawdown of -$8.97, 53.2% win rate, and a 0.46 sharpe ratio. One backtest was just the start though: I ran 99 more varying the entry price floor and ceiling and did some other tests on top of that. Of the 100 backtests, 99 of them came back with a positive pnl. The best one came back with +$266.35 PnL, max drawdown of -$12.72, 65.48% win rate, and a 1.29 sharpe ratio. The weakest one had a -$1.02 PnL, max drawdown of -$$7.83, 42.11% win rate, and a 0.03 sharpe ratio.  
  
Beyond just the backtests, I ran a parameter sensitivity test which mapped all the results of the backtests based on the two varied parameters (price entry floor and ceiling). The price floors varied from 5¢ to 59¢ and ceilings from 60¢ to 95¢ and the 28¢ floor and 71¢ ceiling was the combination that performed the best. This test creates a 3D curve whose shape is telling about wether the winning parameters performed well because it was a one off lucky setting or not. The curve is broad smooth ridge without any spikes i.e nearby parameters perform similarly which is a great result.  
  
I also ran a permutation test which reshuffled the timing of the Coinbase data and reruns the 100 variants on that shuffled data. A backtest could come back positive because the signals that the strategy uses line up with profitable trades rather than because of an actual edge the strategy has discovered. This test checks if that was the case and none of the 100 reshuffled backtests matched the original result which suggests the positive backtests were not due to chanced alignment.  
  
The results from these tests make me feel better about this strategy and also show much profit gets negatively affected as the price floor is raised. The next step will be validating the version with the winning parameter settings in a paper trading session, and then real life execution with guardrails in place before scaling up.
